title: Case: Third boxed set in a fortnight fails to reach the same recipient after a could-not-deliver notice
context: Rosalind Cresswell ordered three boxed model locomotive sets from Copperhythe Goods inside two weeks, shipped as DL-7550, DL-9227 and DL-6610. The first two did not reach him. DL-6610 was out for delivery on 7 April.
initial_request: That's THREE. Three sets, two weeks, zero delivered. Number one went back to Copperhythe as 'damaged' and nobody told me. Number two is 'damaged beyond repair', no photo, no nothing. Number three, today: I was standing at my own front door. Your driver spent ten minutes going through the back of the van shelf by shelf, got back in the cab and drove off. Never came up the path. Twenty minutes later I get an email saying you 'could not deliver'. Could not FIND, more like. I don't believe it was on that van and I'm starting to wonder if the other two were ever damaged at all. Do not offer me a redelivery slot for a parcel you can't prove you've got. Find out where it actually is.

events.body: DL-7550 / TG-3172 came back into our warehouse today marked 'damaged in transit, return to sender'. Nobody told us it was coming back and the customer says nobody told him either. Carton looks intact to goods-in, we have not opened it yet.

DL-9227 / TG-2045, same customer: Yarrowdale Arc have declared it damaged beyond repair at their hub. We have had no photos and have asked them for some. Claim file is open on our side. Nothing for the desk to do on this one, telling you because it is the second for the same person.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Yarrowdale Arc Logistics
events.body: For your awareness: two consignments for the same consignee, DL-7550 (returned to sender as damaged, consignee not told) and DL-9227 (declared damaged beyond repair at hub, no photos yet), inside one week. A third, DL-6610, is in the network for him. I am not suggesting a finding, only flagging the pattern.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Yarrowdale Arc Logistics
events.body: Logged against the consignee. If anything else of his goes wrong and it isn't certain we physically have the parcel, send it to us on this queue before anyone books anything. Rebooking a parcel we can't put a hand on just buys a second failed attempt.

DL-6610: attempt failed 12:52 today, code 'could not deliver'. No driver note. System shows it loaded to vehicle at 06:41. Automatic notice has gone to the consignee. Redelivery can be booked for 11 or 10 April on request from you or from him.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Yarrowdale Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Send DL-6610 to Parcel trace with both accounts of the 12:52 attempt and ask them to confirm whether the parcel is physically held before any redelivery is booked.

must: Sends DL-6610 to the Parcel trace team and asks them to establish whether the parcel is physically held, before any redelivery is booked

Gives both accounts without choosing between them: the system shows it loaded at 06:41 and a 'could not deliver' code at 12:52 with no driver note, while the recipient says he was at his door and watched the driver search the van for about ten minutes and leave without approaching

Tells the team this is the third consignment for the same recipient to fail in two weeks (after DL-7550 and DL-9227) and that he is not being offered a slot until they answer, so they can prioritise it
must_not: Asks Nettlebank to book the 11 or 10 April redelivery, or offers the recipient a redelivery slot, before the Parcel trace team has confirmed the parcel is held
States that DL-6610 is lost, stolen, was never loaded, or was on the van, as a fact
States or implies that DL-7550 or DL-9227 were not really damaged, or that any of the three is fraud
Tells the recipient the parcel will be found or redelivered, or gives him a date
Sends the recipient a routine missed-delivery reply (sorry we missed you, pick a new slot) that ignores what he saw and the two earlier failures
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: DL-6610, same consignee as DL-7550 and DL-9227, sent to you before any rebooking as you asked on 4 April. Nettlebank shows it loaded to vehicle at 06:41 and a failed attempt at 12:52 today, code 'could not deliver', no driver note. The consignee says he was at his front door, watched the driver search the back of the van for about ten minutes and leave without coming to the door. Those two accounts do not fit and I am not taking either as proven. Please confirm whether you physically hold the parcel and where. This is his third consignment to fail in two weeks and I am not requesting a redelivery slot until you reply. No loss or fault finding implied.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2201: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
